newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg shares up on Q4 EPS, outlook.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg shares up on Q4 EPS, outlook.

text.p: Kellogg Co shares rose 1-3/8 at 69-3/8 after the company posted slightly higher fourth quarter operating earnings and continued to project a low double-digit percentage increase in 1997 earnings, analysts said.
The earnings and the outlook may have triggered some short covering in the stock, analysts added.
"It's more likely that the (reason for the stock rise) is that the company feels it can hit double-digit earnings growth for 1997 versus 1996," BT Securities analyst John O'Neil said.
In November, Kellogg said it expects earnings for 1997 to be up by a low double-digit percentage compared with 1996.
"We continue to expect low double-digit earnings per share growth," Kellogg spokesman Richard Lovell said.
Earlier, Kellogg reported fourth quarter earnings before charges of $0.78 a share, up from $0.77 a year ago. For the year, it earned $3.07 a share, down from $3.48 a year ago, both before charges.
The current First Call consensus for 1997 earnings is $3.40 a share, up about 10.7 percent from 1996.
Lovell added that Kellogg continues to expect earnings for the first quarter to be down compared with the $0.99 it earned in the first quarter of 1996.
He added the decline could be "significant," but did not quantify the decline.
